A pale turquoise, fast-flowing river winds through a vast abandoned stone city, dividing dense districts of ruins on both banks. The rugged mountain valley presses around it in broad rock shelves, cliffs, large pale boulders, gullies, and steep enclosing ridges, with uneven brown earth between the rock.

Dozens upon dozens of roofless medieval buildings follow narrow dirt lanes organically, alongside irregular courtyards, and stepped rocky ground. They crowd closest beside the river and thin toward the surrounding slopes. Weathered gray masonry shapes squat rectangular houses, taller blocky halls, broken towers, and several larger Gothic structures with pointed and rounded arches, arcades, buttress-like wall sections, and partially collapsed upper stories. Most retain only jagged exterior walls and exposed room divisions; a few preserve decayed timber frames, beams, balconies, or skeletal roofs.

A narrow arched stone bridge joins the banks. Scattered stairs, retaining walls, rubble piles, fallen logs, and isolated masonry fragments lie among the ruins. Irregular clusters of mature leafy trees, sparse woodland, scrub, grasses, weeds, and small wildflowers fill open spaces and settlement edges, leaving a few broad bare courtyards within the denser blocks.

Beyond the city, rocky, lightly forested mountains continue under low white clouds and mist threading between slopes and buildings. Soft daylight holds a quiet, hazy, overgrown atmosphere. The sprawling city stays tightly packed and distinctly unordered, its architecture following the natural rock rather than a grid.
